tickets.title: Prepare mortgage liquidity source analysis for Nettlewhisk
tickets.text: Prepare a mortgage liquidity source analysis for Julian and Iris Nettlewhisk comparing Teacup Comet Bank cash, short-term bond holdings, the Velvet Acorn Custody joint brokerage, and Julian's vested Cloudberry Kite Robotics shares, preserving the $80,000 post-closing reserve target.
tickets.evidence: Julian asked for a mortgage liquidity source analysis comparing bank cash, short-term bond holdings, taxable brokerage sales, and vested employer shares to fund the remaining down payment while preserving the stated reserve target; the agreed follow-up is due 2025-10-08.

tickets.title: Upload bank and brokerage statements to lender portal
tickets.text: Upload the most recent Teacup Comet Bank statement and Velvet Acorn Custody brokerage statement to the lender's underwriting portal for Julian and Iris Nettlewhisk, and document the $25,000 earnest money withdrawal from the Teacup Comet Bank checking account.
tickets.evidence: the lender’s portal shows the most recent Teacup Comet Bank statement and Velvet Acorn Custody brokerage statement have not been uploaded, and the underwriter is asking for documentation tying the earnest money withdrawal to the source account; this remains needed by 2025-10-06.

tickets.title: Review cash-flow effect of rate-lock alternatives
tickets.text: Review the cash-flow effect of the rate-lock alternatives for Julian and Iris Nettlewhisk's $945,000 Portland townhouse purchase, comparing the options against their $9,600 monthly household spending and the $5,850 preliminary mortgage estimate including escrow, before Julian responds.
tickets.evidence: The mortgage contact sent updated loan terms with a rate-lock choice and financing contingency timeline, and Julian wants the cash-flow effect of the lock alternatives reviewed before he responds; the agreed review is due 2025-10-10.

tickets.title: Resolve student loan payment discrepancy in mortgage file
tickets.text: Resolve the student loan payment discrepancy in Julian and Iris Nettlewhisk's mortgage file by confirming with Iris's servicer that her current income-driven federal student loan payment is $410 per month, so underwriting reflects the correct figure rather than the $640 listed.
tickets.evidence: the mortgage application lists Iris’s student loan payment as $640 per month, while the current servicer statement provided by Iris shows a $410 income-driven payment, creating a different debt-to-income calculation for underwriting; resolution remains needed by 2025-10-07.

tickets.title: Refresh Velvet Acorn Custody aggregation feed in planning portal
tickets.text: Refresh the Velvet Acorn Custody aggregation feed in the planning portal so the liquidity worksheet reflects the current joint brokerage balance, including cash and short-term bond positions available for closing on Julian and Iris Nettlewhisk's Portland townhouse purchase.
tickets.evidence: The Velvet Acorn Custody aggregation feed in the planning portal is showing a stale joint brokerage balance, so the liquidity worksheet is not reflecting the current cash and short-term bond positions available for closing; the agreed follow-up is due 2025-10-06.

tickets.title: Coordinate new-home insurance and liability coverage
tickets.text: Coordinate new-home insurance and liability coverage for Julian and Iris Nettlewhisk's Portland townhouse purchase, replacing their current renters-only policy set with appropriate property and liability coverage for the new property before closing.
tickets.evidence: The townhouse purchase changes the household’s property and liability exposure, and the couple has only renters coverage in place through their current policy set; the agreed new-home insurance and liability coordination is due 2025-10-15.

tickets.title: Review tax lots in taxable ETF positions
tickets.text: Review the tax lots in the taxable ETF positions in Julian and Iris Nettlewhisk's joint Velvet Acorn Custody brokerage account, identifying which holdings have short-term gain lots versus lower-gain long-term lots to determine the most suitable positions for closing cash.
tickets.evidence: Lena noted that several taxable ETF positions have both short-term gain lots and lower-gain long-term lots, affecting which holdings may be most suitable if brokerage assets are used for closing cash; the agreed tax-lot review is due 2025-10-09.
